**[One who was testified against that he seeks to forge, and in it are 3 seifim]:**
Witnesses who testified regarding Reuven that he came to request of them that they forge a deed of a maneh against Shimon, and afterwards he produced a deed of a maneh against Shimon—one does not collect with it, and his claim is only like an oral claim, and we do not pay heed to the deed even if it is validated in beit din, until the witnesses of the deed testify that they wrote it and signed it, or others testify that they saw that they signed. However, that which they or others testify that they recognize their signatures is of no benefit, for since he is suspected of forging, we fear perhaps he forged their signatures to the extent that it truly appears to them that it is their signature. And there are those who say that if the witnesses of the deed themselves recognize their signatures, it is a validation, because they themselves would recognize if they forged their signatures. And for the law, one should be concerned for the first opinion. But if combined with this they also remember the loan, the deed is valid; and with the memory of the loan alone we do not validate the deed, for perhaps it was only an oral loan and he forged it to make it a loan by deed.

Other documents found in his possession are not disqualified, and even regarding this Shimon, if another document was found with him that was not for this amount, it is not disqualified. The reason is that every person is presumed to have a status of fitness, and we suspend judgment, assuming that he has an oral loan against Shimon and sought to make it a loan with a document; therefore, we do not have the power to disqualify other validated documents. A proof for this is that he only requested of the witnesses to make for him one for the amount of a maneh. Nevertheless, his document requires much inquiry and investigation, since in any event he has been established as a forger [it appears to me]. And if the witnesses testified that he requested of them to make a forged document against Shimon and did not mention the amount, all of his documents against Shimon are presumed to be forged. And if he requested of them generally to make a forged document and did not mention the name of Shimon, all of his documents are presumed to be forged [as is implied by the Rosh, chapter 3 of Ketubot, siman 3; see there, for the wording is somewhat garbled and it should be read as "and furthermore," and delve into this].

When we said that the document is invalid, nevertheless we do not tear it, for perhaps he will bring witnesses who saw that they signed; and also we do not leave the document in his hand, for perhaps he or his heirs will collect with it in another beit din that did not know that he wished to forge, but rather we leave it in the hand of a trustee. And if he seized property from the borrower with this document in the presence of witnesses, such that he does not have a migo of "I did not take," we remove it from his hand, for until its fitness is clarified, it is presumed to be invalid. And if he produced a document that witnesses saw in his hand prior to that time when he was seeking to forge, the document is not invalidated retroactively, for at that time it was still under the presumption of fitness; and specifically when it was validated in a beit din prior to this time [Shach].
